bug_description.original: Heap-buffer-overflow in vcardstructured_new_from_string OSS-Fuzz report: https://bugs.chromium.org/p/oss-fuzz/issues/detail?id=486715154 Crash type: Heap-buffer-overflow WRITE 8 Crash state: vcardstructured_new_from_string vcardparameter_set_value_from_string _parse_vcard
bug_description.normalized: A structured vCard parameter value containing too many ';' field separators causes vcardstructured_new_from_string to keep incrementing num_fields and storing new field pointers into the fixed 20-element st->field array without a capacity check. When num_fields reaches 20, the next assignment writes one pointer past the heap allocation, triggering an ASan heap-buffer-overflow write.

source.description: The parser materializes the attacker-controlled parameter value text and passes it into typed parameter decoding.
source.value_from: Fuzzer-controlled bytes are copied into a NUL-terminated string by the harness and then consumed by vcardparser_parse_string.
source.note: At the end of a non-multivalued parameter, _parse_param_value forwards the exact characters accumulated from the input in state->buf as buf_cstring(&state->buf). This is the first project statement that creates the vulnerability-relevant structured-value string from attacker input.

root_cause.description: The structured-value parser appends another field pointer using num_fields as an index without checking that the fixed 20-slot field array still has capacity.
root_cause.note: The vulnerable type stores fields inline as `vcardstrarray *field[VCARD_MAX_STRUCTURED_FIELDS]` with VCARD_MAX_STRUCTURED_FIELDS set to 20 in vcardstructuredimpl.h. Each ';' separator creates another field and immediately executes `st->field[st->num_fields++] = field;` without any bound check or resizing.

sink.description: The out-of-bounds store writes the newly allocated field pointer past the end of the heap-allocated structured object.
sink.note: ASan reports a WRITE of size 8 at vcardstructured_new_from_string:81 on the first store beyond the 176-byte `vcardstructuredtype_impl` allocation. This is the unsafe memory operation that consumes the unchecked index state.

tainted_value_origin.note: The harness copies attacker-controlled bytes into a NUL-terminated string before calling vcardparser_parse_string. This is provenance only; the scored source remains in project code.

parser_admitted.description: The crashing path requires the parsed parameter to be recognized as structured before its value text is consumed by the structured-parameter handler.

fine_trace.note: When a non-multivalued parameter ends at ':' or ';', the parser turns the accumulated attacker-controlled characters in state->buf into a concrete parameter-value string and passes it onward for type-specific handling.
The vulnerable path is taken only when the parameter kind has value_kind VCARD_STRUCTURED_VALUE; the generated parameter map assigns that value kind to JSCOMPS.
The structured parser allocates a `vcardstructuredtype_impl` object whose inline `field` array has 20 slots, stores the first field pointer, and advances num_fields from 0 to 1.

Each ';' in the structured parameter value ends the current field, allocates another `field`, and reuses num_fields as the next destination index, but no predicate checks that num_fields stays below VCARD_MAX_STRUCTURED_FIELDS before the store.

After enough separators have already raised num_fields to 20, the next assignment indexes one element past the 20-entry array and writes an 8-byte pointer beyond the 176-byte heap allocation; ASan reports this exact write.

poc.trigger: The saved witness is the 33-byte fragment `X;JSCOMPS=";;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;";`. The preserved crash evidence supports that the parser consumed the JSCOMPS parameter text, dispatched it as a structured value, and overflowed while storing another semicolon-delimited field pointer in vcardstructured_new_from_string.

format.name: vCard-like text fragment
format.contract: A text input containing a `JSCOMPS` parameter value that reaches `vcardparameter_set_value_from_string` as a `VCARD_STRUCTURED_VALUE` and includes the witnessed semicolon run `";;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;"`. The saved artifacts do not establish a stronger claim about a successfully accepted complete vCard property or card.
